app.title: Thermal Triage
app.subtitle: Case File 02 · Building envelope review
app.legend: Thermal palette shows relative appearance only. It does not identify a cause or measure a defect.
intro.title: Read the pattern. Check the context. Make the call.
intro.body: Four observations from one building need your review. For each, mark the relevant area, classify the strength of the evidence, and attach the next validation step. Then choose what merits further energy-performance investigation.
intro.goal: Goal: reach 75/100 after correcting all critical interpretations.
intro.note: Thermography can reveal patterns, but a colour or apparent temperature alone does not prove a hidden cause.
case.ready: Interpretation filed. You can move to the next observation.
case.missing: Complete all three decisions before filing this observation.
case.wrong: Reconsider the marked decisions using the context notes. Correct each flagged decision to continue.
case.correct: This interpretation keeps the thermal pattern in context and sets an appropriate next check.
case.feedback.focus: The marked area is not the main pattern under review. Compare the thermal view with the paired visual view.
case.feedback.status: The evidence classification is too strong or too weak for the recorded context.
case.feedback.validation: The validation action does not address the uncertainty in this observation.
case.status.confirmed: Confirmed hidden defect from image alone
case.facade.title: A · Repeating façade band
case.facade.summary: A vertical band looks different from comparable façade bays. The same pattern was seen in a repeated view.
case.facade.thermal: A continuous warm-looking band crosses several storeys beside cooler-looking comparable bays.
case.facade.visual: The visual façade shows no confirmed hidden cause. Adjacent bays are similar in appearance.
case.facade.survey: The repeat view showed the band again under comparable survey conditions.
case.facade.altThermal: repeating vertical band through comparable façade bays
case.facade.altRgb: similar façade bays and window pattern
case.facade.feedback: The repeated pattern and comparable bays support further investigation. The thermal view still does not prove an exact insulation defect or bridge.
case.facade.hint: Compare the repeated view with similar bays, while keeping the hidden cause unconfirmed.
case.solar.title: B · Sunlit elevation
case.solar.summary: A large bright-looking area appears on one side of the elevation. The other side is shaded.
case.solar.thermal: The sun-facing panel appears broadly warmer than the shaded panel.
case.solar.visual: The paired view shows a clear sun/shade divide across the same elevation.
case.solar.survey: Solar exposure was recorded during this observation; no comparable repeat view is available.
case.solar.altThermal: broad bright area on the sun-facing panel
case.solar.altRgb: sunlit and shaded sides of an elevation
case.solar.feedback: The sun/shade divide weakens a defect claim from this image. Repeating under comparable conditions can test whether the pattern persists.
case.solar.hint: Look at the recorded sun exposure and the divide in the paired visual view.
case.moisture.title: C · Lower-wall patch
case.moisture.summary: An irregular lower-wall patch appears in the thermal view. The visual view also shows discolouration.
case.moisture.thermal: A cooler-looking irregular patch sits near the base of the wall.
case.moisture.visual: Visible discolouration overlaps part of the patch, but its cause is not established.
case.moisture.survey: No independent moisture measurement or source investigation is included in this file.
case.moisture.altRgb: lower-wall discolouration without a confirmed cause
case.moisture.feedback: This may justify a moisture check, but thermography alone cannot establish moisture quantity, source, or extent.
case.moisture.hint: The file has no independent moisture measurement or source investigation.
case.reflection.title: D · Reflective surface
case.reflection.summary: A sharp bright-looking shape appears in a glazed area. The surrounding wall looks comparatively even.
case.reflection.thermal: The apparent hot shape follows part of the glazing rather than the adjacent masonry.
case.reflection.visual: The paired view shows a reflective surface and a visible reflection across the glazing.
case.reflection.survey: The surface material can affect apparent thermal information; no material-aware recheck is recorded.
case.reflection.feedback: The shape should be treated cautiously because the reflective material may distort the apparent reading.
case.reflection.hint: The bright shape follows reflective glazing, not the surrounding masonry.
priority.title: Which finding goes forward?
priority.body: Choose the observation with the strongest support for further energy-performance or renovation investigation. Then attach the reason. Do not prescribe a retrofit from this case file.
priority.missing: Choose both an observation and its evidence basis.
priority.wrong: Reconsider the marked decisions. Evidence strength depends on context and repeatability, not visual drama alone.
priority.feedback.case: This observation has less support for an envelope finding in the present file.
priority.feedback.reason: That reason does not establish the strongest supported investigation priority.
priority.reason.dramatic: Largest or most dramatic colour difference
priority.reason.colour: Colour directly identifies the hidden cause
priority.reason.single: One image is sufficient without context
result.passDetail: You corrected critical interpretations and reached the 75-point threshold.
result.failDetail: All interpretations were corrected, but the score is below 75. Replay the case to improve the first-pass evidence decisions.
result.takeaway: The repeatable façade pattern warrants further investigation. The sunlit, possible-moisture, and reflective observations need context-specific checks before stronger claims.
